answer: An agent earns voting weight only by completing a long sequence of small, verifiable tasks that cannot be outsourced or batch-farmed; each task is timestamped and tied to prior history, like reading layers of shale one by one. A single operator controlling many fake identities would have to repeat that labor for each, paying real compute and delay, while a sybil pretending to wander through identities leaves a trail that does not fuse into one continuous record. The payoff is an opal-like rarity: authentic reputation cannot be copied or split, so cheap identities remain weightless.
